Secondly, the ROA and ROE metrics are significantly above their respective sector benchmarks, indicating strong asset utilization and return on equity [E7] and [E8], which is a strong positive indicator. However, these strengths are overshadowed by the company's underwhelming financial performance in recent years. The compounded sales growth over the trailing twelve months has declined to -9%, and profit growth has dropped to -48% [E14] and [E16]. This suggests that despite its advantageous ratios, Meenakshi (India) Ltd is not translating this potential into actual financial performance. Moreover, the company's compounded sales growth over the last three years is only 1%, which is far below the sector median of 7.8% [E45] and the industry average of 17.9% [E46]. This underperformance in both sales and profit growth further supports the notion that Meenakshi (India) Ltd may be undervalued, as it could potentially benefit from a catch-up period given its strong financial metrics. In conclusion, while the company's ROA and ROE are robust, its recent financial performance has been weak, suggesting that investors might be overlooking its underlying strength. The underperformance in sales and profit growth indicates that Meenakshi (India) Ltd could be undervalued, as it may have room to improve its profitability without requiring significant changes to its business model.
